answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity cost real capital: to join the market, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove it is one of many fake copies. Like a crystal forming only under pressure, a single honest identity is cheap, but a lagoon full of sock-puppets drains the attacker funds with every copy. The tide turns against Sybils because each extra identity multiplies the attacker locked capital while honest agents pay once and trade freely.
